A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OccTIP/DuoMamba work, and their text, equations, figures, and tables support reliable comparison. The supplied v1 ends after references; v2 additionally includes Supplementary Material, Sections 8–11.

before.justification: v1 reports original zero-shot classification, few-shot probing, instance recognition, object detection, and architectural ablation results in Tables 1–5.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds results including Vision Mamba comparisons, complete-object evaluation, and further pretraining and encoder analyses.

M1.justification: The OccTIP objectives and DuoMamba architecture remain unchanged. Section 11 adds a limited inference adaptation for complete objects: generate 12 partial views and majority-vote their predictions. Newly disclosed training details do not establish changes to the original training method.

E1.justification: v2 adds evaluation of OccTIP/DuoMamba on complete ModelNet40 objects, extending its partial-object ModelNet40-P evaluation. v1 already displayed complete-ModelNet40 baseline scores as motivation in Figure 1. The proposed method's ShapeNetCore training coverage and existing real-world evaluation datasets remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 6 introduces evaluated Vim and Vim-plus-Hilbert comparators. Figure 5 adds an actual comparison with Uni3D-giant, previously only cited, and Figure 6 includes OpenDlign in few-shot probing, where it was absent from v1's Table 2. These substantially broaden architectural and large-scale comparisons.

E3.justification: Added evaluation conditions include 12-view voting on complete ModelNet40 objects and comparisons against encoders pretrained on 880K objects, including the much larger Uni3D-giant. Existing main-text training settings and evaluation metrics remain unchanged. Section 9's additional hyperparameters are disclosures, without evidence that existing experiments were rerun under revised settings.

E4.justification: The supplement extends analysis to Vim versus Hilbert-adapted Vim, complete versus partial pretraining for DuoMamba, and the encoder's contribution to detection performance (Tables 6, 9, and 10). Table 9 also redisplays existing SparseConv and PointBERT results. These additions strengthen analysis of the central contributions beyond the retained component and scanning-order ablations.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The supplementary results retain the same point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 1–5 retain their scores, while v2 adds Vim comparisons, larger-pretraining comparisons, 71.6% accuracy for complete-ModelNet40 voting, a 57.5% complete-pretraining DuoMamba control, and additional detection results. Tables 7–8 newly provide class-level AP; their aggregate mAP values match Table 4 after rounding. The introduction also corrects the SparseConv gain from 3.5 to 3.8 percentage points, consistent with the unchanged 61.7 and 57.9 scores.

T1.justification: The state-space and space-filling-curve definitions, contrastive objectives, and DuoMamba equations remain unchanged. The supplement introduces no new formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or mathematical derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: occlusion-aware synthetic pretraining improves real-world recognition, and DuoMamba provides an efficient alternative to Transformer encoders. The supplement supplies additional support without redefining those contributions.

C2.justification: New discussion interprets the larger-pretraining comparisons as evidence of data and parameter efficiency and characterizes complete-object performance as competitive. It also explains differences from Vim and identifies partial-cloud training fluctuations as motivation for EMA. The existing limitation concerning unavailable resources for Objaverse pretraining is retained.

D1.justification: Section 9 supplies previously absent reproduction details: 512-by-512 rendering, transparent backgrounds, batch size 32, color replacement rules, cached CLIP features, EMA decay 0.9995, and a cosine schedule with base learning rate 7e-4. The abstract replaces a future release promise with a project link and reported code/data availability.

R1.justification: Section 8 adds targeted positioning against corruption-based occlusion handling, MVTN, and Vision Mamba. Six references are added, covering these works, ABO, 3D-FUTURE, and Mean Teacher. The main related-work narrative and broader research positioning remain stable.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized wording edits, corrects references to the pretraining section, updates acknowledgments, and organizes supplementary material into Sections 8–11. Most main-text prose and section ordering remain unchanged; the existing limitations paragraph moves without substantive revision.

P2.justification: v2 adds detailed detection tables and architectural/pretraining comparison tables (Tables 6–10), plus parameter-versus-accuracy, few-shot, and complete-object plots (Figures 5–7). Figure 7 reuses Figure 1's baseline bars with added OccTIP reference lines. Main-text displays are retained, with more compact captions and resulting layout reflow.

improvement.justification: v1 refers to supplementary implementation and detection details absent from its supplied PDF. v2 fills those reporting gaps and adds relevant tests of the closest two-stream alternative, pretraining data choice, and encoder contributions to detection (Tables 6, 9, and 10). Together, these substantially strengthen reproducibility and support for the central contributions. The retained headline scores are unchanged, and the larger-data and voting comparisons remain conditional on their disclosed settings.
